chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the thief: When he is seized and he has taken the goods, and he is in the house and has not yet come out, so he said: There is no cutting upon him until he comes out with it from the house.
ai.seo_question: When does the punishment of hand amputation for theft begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic definition of 'taking possession' (qabd) in theft law, specifying that the hadd punishment is contingent upon the thief successfully removing the goods from the confines of the dwelling. This condition distinguishes between mere possession inside the home and the completed act of theft, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise legal criteria for applying fixed punishments. It underscores the principle that the crime is not fully consummated until the stolen item is taken out of the owner's immediate domain.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the thief: ‘When he is seized and he has taken the goods, and he is in the house and not having come out. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no cutting upon him until he comes out with it (the goods) from the house’.
